topic: The Mental Accounting Tax Refund Effect
title: Why you blow tax refunds instantly #Shorts
description: Ever wonder why a tax refund disappears in days while a regular raise just vanishes into savings? In 2000, behavioral economists Eldar Shafir and Richard Thaler proved your brain uses a weird mental trick on unexpected cash. Drop a comment with what you blew your last refund on, and hit subscribe for more money psychology. #MoneyPsychology #PersonalFinance #FinancialTraps
script: Why do you blow unexpected cash instantly while saving your regular paycheck? Behavioral economists Eldar Shafir and Richard Thaler tracked identical income increases in the year 2000. People spent over forty percent of an unexpected tax refund within two weeks, compared to less than five percent of a normal payroll raise. You get an eight hundred dollar tax refund and instantly browse online carts for gear you would never buy with weekly cash. Which one did you blow your last tax refund on, and why is your brain biologically wired this way? Force a forty eight hour cooling off period on windfalls by automatically routing them into a sub-account. This is exactly the kind of trap we track in our Money Psychology series.
